newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Gold - Miners cover as price sinks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Gold - Miners cover as price sinks.

text.p: The downward trend in gold prices has Australian mining companies running for cover.
The need to hedge forward significant portions of future gold production amid a fast-sinking international and Australian-dollar gold price has taken on new urgency, miners say.
Gold continued its retreat on Wednesday as big investment funds led an international exodus from the metal.
COMEX February gold ended down $1.50 an ounce at US$353.20, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at US$352.60.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted US$352.25-US$352.75, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at US$354.45, after gold was fixed at US$352.45 in the morning, the lowest level since October 1993.
The latest price drop has brought gold nearer to a key technical marker of US$350, which if crossed would threaten to accelerate the downward spiral, bullion dealers here believe.
"What we're seeing is some of the big producers selling into a declining market along with the funds, which is not a good sign," one said.
Dealers said local investors found little comfort in indications that Dutch central bank sales of 300 tonnes of gold in favour of currency, confirmed this week, were probably concluded months ago.

"There appears to still be gold in the hands of professionals looking for a home, a dealer said. Market watchers in Australia are reassessing their expectations for gold in 1997 based on its perfomance since the start of the year.

Simon Middleton, gold analyst for the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics, said gold has a better chance for recovery in the second half as robust physical demand for the metal adds its weight to the market.
"I wouldn't write gold off," he said.
For their part, Australian mining houses appear to be absorbing a slow-collapsing gold price.
Normandy Mining Ltd said on Thursday it has hedged 4.628 million ounces on a group basis at an average price of A$740 an ounce to 2006.
Consulting firm Surbiton Associates believes hedging has enabled miners to remain fundamentally sound as gold prices deteriorate.
"We've put in place significant hedge positions," said Peter Lalor, managing director of gold miner Sons of Gwalia Ltd.
Sons of Gwalia lifted the number of ounces it has sold forward to 3.2 million ounces from 1.7 million previously.
The sales are spread out but ensure an average return of about A$640 an ounce. This compares favourably with a spot price of about A$458 an ounce.
Lalor said production costs averaging A$352 an ounce provided further protection from the actual gold price, adding steps were being taken to reduce cost further over the next six months.
Low operating costs also aided Aurora Gold Ltd which is mining in the rich Kalimantan region of Indonesia.
Production costs at Aurora's Mount Muro mine dropped to US$199.00 an ounce in the fourth quarter of calendar 1996 from US$213.00 in the previous three months, the company said on Thursday.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
